evals.name: sales-cockpit-from-scratch
evals.prompt: Build a React sales rep cockpit page: a table of open deals (deal name, account, stage, amount, close date, owner) plus 3 KPI tiles above it (pipeline value, win rate, avg deal size). Use Tailwind and Inter as the font. Make it look sharp, not like a generic AI-generated dashboard.
evals.expected_output: A React/Tailwind component using Inter for labels/nav/body, but numeric columns (amount, KPI values) use a tabular-figure or monospaced treatment. Badges/pills for deal stage are rationed to one consistent style, not a different pill shape per element type. Accent color is not the terracotta/#D97757 or acid-green-on-black AI-default palette. Density is appropriate for a power-user tool (not oversized whitespace).

evals.name: review-existing-dashboard
evals.prompt:
Here's our internal ops dashboard component (React + Tailwind, Inter font). It feels a bit 'AI-generated' but I can't put my finger on why. Can you review it and tell me what to change? ```tsx export function OpsDashboard({ rows }: { rows: Row[] }) { return (

Active Jobs

142

Failed Today

7

Success Rate

96.4%

{rows.map(r => ( ))}
JobStatusDurationOwner
{r.name} {r.status} {r.duration} {r.owner}
); } ```
evals.expected_output: Points out concrete tells from the pasted code: every status AND owner wrapped in the same rounded-pill shape (should not both be pills — owner name doesn't need a badge at all), numeric/duration columns rendered as plain Inter with no tabular-figure treatment, hierarchy relying on color alone (orange/green) for KPI tiles rather than weight/size too. Gives specific before/after suggestions, not generic praise or a rewrite of the whole thing unprompted.

evals.name: vague_make_it_look_good
evals.prompt: I'm building an internal admin panel for our support team to triage tickets (Inter font, Tailwind, list of tickets with priority/status/assignee). Just want it to look good and not screams 'made by AI', what should I keep in mind?
evals.expected_output: Applies the skill's checklist to this specific context (dense internal tool, priority/status/assignee columns) rather than giving generic design advice unrelated to Inter/typography. Mentions rationing pill/badge usage across priority vs status vs assignee, tabular figures if there are any numeric/id columns, the known AI-default accent palette to avoid, and that density should stay tight for a support-triage power tool rather than adding marketing-style whitespace.
